<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">to</font>
improve system functionality or network services to make their network more
effective (&#147;Enhancement Services&#148;). The fees received for up-front services and
certain Enhancement Services are deferred and recognized as revenue ratably
over the term of the contract or the expected life of the customer
relationship, whichever is longer, as these fees do not represent the
culmination of a separate earnings process.&#160;
We also receive a monthly service fee to provide the ongoing data
management services required to keep the records current for all subscribers,
to maintain and monitor network components and to support and maintain the
software and systems required to provide the services. The fees received for
these monthly services are recognized as revenue in the period in which all of
the above criteria have been met, which is generally the month services are
provided. For data management services we perform under our outsourced or
licensed model, customers do not have a contractual right to take possession of
our software; therefore, we account for these arrangements as service
contracts.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maintenance contracts are sold to customers
that either purchase or possess database and call handling systems. The fees
received for ongoing maintenance obligations are deferred and recognized as
revenue over the contractual term of the arrangement.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Systems and new products revenue represents
revenue recognized from the sales of new database and call handling systems as
well as customized solutions sold to existing customers. Software license
revenue and related hardware sales are recognized upon execution of a contract
and completion of delivery obligations, provided that no uncertainties exist
regarding customer acceptance and that collection of the related receivable is
reasonably assured.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Professional services revenue is generated by
providing consulting services and is recognized in the period in which all of
the above criteria have been met.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In certain situations involving the delivery
of products with significant customization or modification services, we also
recognize revenue on a percentage-of-completion basis, as prescribed by
SOP&nbsp;81-1, &#147;Accounting for Performance of Construction-Type and Certain
Production-Type Contracts.&#148; In these situations, we develop and utilize
estimates to ratably recognize costs and revenue as work is completed relative
to the total estimated time and costs to complete projects. Delays in
completing projects or significant changes to original cost estimates could
adversely impact future periods in that additional costs or amortization
periods for both revenue and expenses may be necessary. When reasonable
estimates cannot be determined at the onset of an agreement due to unique
acceptance criteria or other factors, revenue is recognized on a completed
contract basis.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>When the
software is available for general release;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The expected
benefits to be derived from the software product;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The useful life
of the software product; and</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The future
recoverability of the capitalized amounts.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In assessing the recoverability of our
existing capitalized software assets, we rely on estimates and judgments to
determine the net realizable value of each product. When evaluating the net
realizable value of a given product, we prepare a forward-looking business case
that includes an assessment of future expected benefits to be derived from the
asset. The expected benefits are compared to the direct costs associated with
the delivery and ongoing support of the product to arrive at a contribution
margin, defined as expected benefits less direct costs. This contribution
margin is compared to the current carrying value of the asset at the reporting
date. If the contribution margin exceeds the current asset carrying value plus
any additional investments, such as hardware or additional development required
to enhance or maintain the product, no impairment is recorded. If the
contribution margin is less than the carrying value, the asset carrying value
is impaired to equal the expected contribution margin. Our ability to estimate
future expected benefits to be derived from the asset, with a measured degree
of probability, is the most significant factor in our impairment analysis. If
our ability to estimate the expected benefits changes significantly in any
given period, we could record impairment charges for certain assets.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each quarter, we also assess the expected
benefit period of the assets and amortize the related assets over the expected
benefit period. If our estimate of benefit period is impacted, we could adjust
our estimated amortization periods accordingly, having either a positive or
negative impact on earnings in the period the estimate is changed. In 2004 we
recorded $2.3 million in software impairment charges.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Long-Lived Assets</font></u></i></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We assess the impairment of identifiable
intangibles or long-lived assets, including property and equipment and
goodwill, annually or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances
indicate that the carrying value of the asset may not be recoverable. Factors
we consider important which could trigger an impairment review include the
following:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Significant
under-performance relative to historical or projected future operating results;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Significant
changes in the manner of our use of the acquired assets or the strategy of our
overall business;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Significant
negative industry or economic trends;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Significant
decline in our stock price for a sustained period; or</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Our market
capitalization relative to net book value.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">When we determine that the carrying value of
intangibles or long-lived assets may not be recoverable based on the existence
of one or more of the above indicators of impairment, we measure any impairment
based on the estimated discounted cash flows expected to result from the use of
the asset and its eventual disposition and compare the result to the asset&#146;s
carrying amount. Any impairment loss recognized represents the excess of the
asset&#146;s carrying value over its estimated fair value.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Allowances</font></u></i></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">may</font>
be required. Deterioration in the financial condition of our current customers
may cause our allowance for doubtful accounts to increase and our future
operating results to be adversely affected. In the normal course of our
business, we may be involved in billing disputes with certain customers. The
resolution of these disputes may result in the granting of credit memos to the

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Deferred Tax Assets</font></u></i></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">We follow SFAS No.&nbsp;109, &#147;Accounting for
Income Taxes&#148; (&#147;SFAS&nbsp;109&#148;). The current provision for income taxes
represents actual or estimated amounts payable or refundable on tax returns
filed each year. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the
estimated future tax effects attributable to the temporary differences between
the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and
their respective tax bases as well as operating loss and tax credit
carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using tax rates
expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary
differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Under SFAS&nbsp;109, the
effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in enacted tax laws
is recognized as an adjustment to the tax provision or benefit in the period of
enactment. The overall change in deferred tax assets and liabilities during the
period is equal to the deferred tax expense or benefit for the period. The
carrying value of deferred tax assets may be reduced by a valuation allowance
if, based upon the judgmental assessment of available evidence, it is deemed
more likely than not that some or all of the deferred tax assets will not be
realizable.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;">&nbsp;</p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">We periodically evaluate our estimates and
judgments related to the recoverability of deferred tax assets as required by
SFAS No.&nbsp;109, &#147;Accounting for Income Taxes&#148; (&#147;SFAS&nbsp;109&#148;). We
currently do not have a reserve against our net deferred tax assets, with the
exception of a valuation allowance of $59,000 that has been recorded against
deferred tax assets in our Intrado International, Ltd. subsidiary. &#160;If expected taxable income is not generated in
future years, it may be necessary to reverse some or all of the tax benefit
recorded, adversely impacting tax expense and net income in the future.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;123
(revised 2004), &#147;Share-Based Payment&#148; (&#147;SFAS 123R&#148;), which replaces SFAS
No.&nbsp;123, &#147;Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation,&#148; (&#147;SFAS&nbsp;123&#148;) and
supersedes APB Opinion No.&nbsp;25, &#147;Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees.&#148;
SFAS&nbsp;123R requires all share-based payments to employees, including grants
of employee stock options, to be recognized in the financial statements based
on their fair values beginning with the first interim or annual period after
June&nbsp;15, 2005. The pro forma disclosures previously permitted under
SFAS&nbsp;123 no longer will be an alternative to financial statement
recognition. We are required to adopt SFAS&nbsp;123R in the third quarter of
fiscal 2005, beginning July 1, 2005. Under SFAS&nbsp;123R, we must determine
the appropriate fair value model to be used for valuing share-based payments,
the amortization method for compensation cost and the transition method to be
used at date of adoption. The transition methods include prospective and
retroactive adoption options. Under the retroactive option, prior periods may
be restated either as of the beginning of the year of adoption or for all
periods presented. The prospective method requires that compensation expense be
recorded for all unvested stock options and restricted stock at the beginning
of the first quarter of adoption of SFAS&nbsp;123R, while the retroactive
methods would record compensation expense for all unvested stock options and
restricted stock beginning with the first period restated. We are evaluating
the requirements of SFAS&nbsp;123R and expect that the adoption of
SFAS&nbsp;123R will have a material impact on our consolidated results of
operations and earnings per share. We have not yet determined the method of
adoption or the effect of adopting SFAS&nbsp;123R, and we have not determined
whether the adoption will result in amounts that are similar to the current pro
forma disclosures under SFAS&nbsp;123.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Total Company</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Revenues</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total revenues increased $11.9&nbsp;million
to $136.5&nbsp;million in 2004. The increase is primarily attributable to
increased revenue in the Wireless unit of $12.5 million.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Wireline</font></i>
revenues decreased $1.9&nbsp;million to $81.9&nbsp;million in 2004:</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Recurring data
management services revenues decreased $4.3 million due to reduced pricing in
our ILEC services unit associated with contract extensions as well as
consolidation of customers in our CLEC unit, which led to volume pricing
discounts for certain customers;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Maintenance for
software enhancements increased $2.0&nbsp;million related to additional
maintenance and pricing increases related to certain customers;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Sales of new
software enhancements and systems decreased $1.0 million due to timing
differences between year-end 2003 and 2004 related to the delivery of software
enhancements; and</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Professional
services revenues increased $1.3 million primarily due to VoIP and IEN products

and software enhancements.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Wireless</font></i>

revenues increased by $1.2 million to $3.1 million in 2004:</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>IntelliCast

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>CDB revenues
increased $141,000 to $534,000 due to additional transaction services revenues
relative to the prior year. In 2004, we received a full-year of transactional
services revenue from certain key customers including AT&amp;T and Vartec.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Costs</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total costs increased $27.0 million to $134.6
million in 2004. The significant areas where costs increased from 2003 include
the following items:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Goodwill and
other asset impairment charges increased by $16.9 million primarily due to a
$14.0 million goodwill impairment charge in the bmd reporting unit, a $1.9
impairment charge related to our CDB product offerings, a $588,000 software
impairment charge in our Wireless unit and a $322,000 impairment charge
associated with certain Palladium intangible assets.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

following factors:</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounts payable and accrued liabilities</font></i>
decreased $1.1 million to $9.8 million in 2004, as a result of timing
differences in the payment of obligations accrued at year-end and a reduction
in the vacation accrual due to usage and forfeiture.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Current portion of capital lease obligations </font></i>decreased
$1.4 million to $1.5 million as a result of payments made in 2004, offset by
reclassifications of long-term lease obligations into current portion.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Notes payable&#151;current</font></i> decreased $4.3
million in 2004. The notes payable were prepaid in full in December 2004.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Deferred contract revenue&#151;short term</font></i>
increased $4.0 million to $19.7 million in 2004, primarily due to the
realization of current year revenue and the reclassification of deferred
revenue from long-term to current liabilities based on our estimated
realization of these revenues in the next year.</p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Long-term
liabilities</font></i> decreased $10.8 million to $11.7 million
in 2004. This decrease is primarily a result of the following factors:</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Notes payable, net of current portion </font></i>decreased
$5.9 million in 2004. We repaid all term notes payable outstanding in 2004 with
the exception of $2.0 million, which represents the minimum required borrowing
level on our line of credit with GE Capital.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Mandatorily redeemable preferred stock payable</font></i>
decreased by $4.2 million as a result of the second of three redemptions made
in June 2004 and reclassification of the third and final payment which is due
in June 2005 to short-term obligations.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Deferred contract revenue&#151;long-term</font></i>
decreased $735,000 in 2004, primarily due to its reclassification to a current
liability, offset by deferral of revenues for new contracts in 2004.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0pt;">Direct costs</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;"> include all costs directly attributable to a
business unit&#146;s operations and revenue-earning activities, including
depreciation and amortization expense for those assets that can be identified
to a specific business unit or product (see Note 11) and goodwill and other
asset impairment losses.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;">&nbsp;</p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0pt;">Indirect business unit costs</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;"> include the costs of business unit support
functions, including sales and marketing, general and administrative and
research and development.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Corporate overhead</font></i>
includes these same costs allocated from corporate to business units based on a
weighted average revenue percentage.</p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Wireline Business
Unit</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue decreased by $1.9&nbsp;million to
$81.9 million in 2004 primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Recurring data
management services revenues decreased $4.3 million due to reduced pricing in
our ILEC services unit associated with contract extensions as well as
consolidation of customers in our CLEC unit which led to volume pricing
discounts for certain customers;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Maintenance for
software enhancements increased $2.0&nbsp;million related to additional
maintenance and pricing increases related to certain customers;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Sales of new
software enhancements and systems decreased $1.0 million due to timing
differences between year-end 2003 and 2004 related to delivery of software
enhancements; and</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Professional
services revenues increased $1.3 million primarily due to VoIP and IEN products
and services and the associated integration efforts with the above sale of
systems and software enhancements.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Direct costs increased by $3.9 million
primarily due to higher cost of goods sold for system sales related to our IEN
product offerings.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indirect expenses&#160; increased $1.2 million to $26.0
million in 2004. This increase is primarily due to increased contract labor and
personnel costs to support new product initiatives such as IEN, 9-1-1 IM and
9-1-1 Plus.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Wireless Business
Unit</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenues increased $12.5&nbsp;million to
$51.5&nbsp;million in 2004 due to increased recurring data management services
revenues of $12.2 million attributable to increased deployments and $2.0
million in revenue from our bmd subsidiary, offset by a reduction in professional
services revenues of $1.6 million.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Direct costs increased by $18.3 million to
$39.9 million in 2004. Costs increased due to a $14.0 million goodwill
impairment charge in our bmd subsidiary, a $588,000 software impairment charge,
the hiring of additional operations staff to support cell site implementations,
increased systems maintenance and $1.8 million of costs attributable to our bmd
subsidiary.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indirect expenses increased by $3.8 million
to $16.0 million in 2004. The increase is due to the addition of product
management, sales and finance personnel to support growth, and $1.1 million of
expenses in our bmd subsidiary.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">New Markets Business
Unit</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">Revenue increased $1.2 million to $3.1
million, primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>IntelliCast
revenues increased $1.1 million to $2.5 million due to previous deployments in
Chicago, Phoenix, New Orleans and other municipalities which increased the
number of records under management relative to the prior year, as well as
revenue from a 2004 trial with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric
Administration; and</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>CDB revenues
increased $141,000 to $534,000 due to additional transaction services revenues
relative to the prior year. In 2004, we received a full-year of transactional
services revenue from certain key customers including AT&amp;T and Vartec.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">Direct costs increased by $1.6 million to
$6.3 million in 2004. The increase is due to $1.9 million of software and other
asset impairment charges in our CDB unit, offset slightly by reductions in
operational personnel expenses as a result of lower than anticipated revenue in
our CDB unit.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indirect expenses decreased by $1.8 million
to $2.7 million in 2004 due to reductions and reassignments of sales and
support personnel due to lower than anticipated revenue in our CDB unit.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Year Ended
December&nbsp;31, 2003 Compared to Year Ended December&nbsp;31, 2002</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Wireline Business
Unit</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue increased by $3.0&nbsp;million to
$83.8&nbsp;million in 2003 primarily due to the following:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Recurring data
management services revenue increased $300,000;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Maintenance for
software enhancements increased $3.0&nbsp;million related to additional
maintenance on software enhancements;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Sales of new
software enhancements and systems decreased $800,000 due to timing differences
between year-end 2002 and 2003 related to delivery of software enhancements;
and</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Professional
services revenues increased $500,000 primarily due to VoIP services and other
projects for CLEC customers.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Direct costs increased $900,000. We were able
to leverage direct costs through consolidation of administrative and management
functions and an increase in productivity in key operating units.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indirect business unit costs decreased
$6.3&nbsp;million to $24.8&nbsp;million in 2003. This decrease is due to
savings realized as a result of a reorganization of general and administrative
support personnel which occurred in the fourth quarter of 2002. We also
realized savings in salary and consulting expenses as a result of a reorganization in our sales and product management teams.
In 2002, we also had higher bad debt expenses due to the accrual for potential
bad debt write-offs for certain CLEC customers, most notably MCI (formerly
known as WorldCom,&nbsp;Inc.) which did not occur at the same level in 2003.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Wireless Business
Unit</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue increased by $13.1&nbsp;million to
$39.0&nbsp;million in 2003 due to an increase in cell site deployments and
sales of enhancements for new and existing products, such as EES and PDE.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Direct costs increased by $6.8&nbsp;million
to $21.6&nbsp;million in 2003. Costs increased due to the hiring of additional
operations staff to support cell site implementations and increased systems
maintenance and circuit costs to accommodate growth. Direct costs decreased
slightly as a percentage of revenue, from 57% to 55%, primarily due to
economies of scale associated with the increase in cell sites under management
and the resulting increased revenue base.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indirect business unit costs increased by
$1.0&nbsp;million to $12.2&nbsp;million in 2003. The increase in expense is due
to the addition of product management, sales and finance personnel to support
growth. The decrease as a percentage of revenue, from 43% to 31%, is primarily
due to economies of scale associated with the revenue increase.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">New Markets Business
Unit</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue increased $800,000 to
$1.8&nbsp;million, primarily due to increases in records under IntelliCast
management and an increase in sales by the CDB Group.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Direct costs increased by $1.9&nbsp;million
to $4.6&nbsp;million in 2003. The $1.9&nbsp;million increase due to data
acquisition costs, increases in operational personnel expenses and amortization
of the software development expenditures related to the development of
IntelliCast and CDB product offerings.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indirect business unit costs increased by
$1.8&nbsp;million to $4.6&nbsp;million in 2003. The increase in indirect
business unit costs is due to the addition of sales and support personnel, as
well as increased marketing and advertising costs for IntelliCast and CDB product
offerings.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Corporate Overhead</font></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Corporate
overhead, consisting of expenses incurred by various corporate support units,
decreased by $3.7&nbsp;million.</font> This decrease was
primarily due to a $4.7&nbsp;million asset impairment charge in 2002 that did
not occur in 2003, offset by increases in general and administrative costs due
to the increased payroll, benefit, insurance and legal costs as outlined
earlier.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><b><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Operating
Activities</font></u></i></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">Our ability to generate cash from operations is primarily a function of
our ability to continue to generate net income, improve our collection efforts
on outstanding accounts receivable and execute sound cash management related to
accounts payable.&#160; Our ability to
generate operating income is primarily a function of increased revenue without
a corresponding increase in our cash expenses. From 2003 to 2004, our revenue
increased from $124.7 million to $136.5 million, a 10% increase. For the same
period, our total operating expenses increased 25%, from $107.6 million in 2003
to $134.6 million in 2004. However, our total operating expenses in 2004
include $16.9 million in non-cash asset impairment charges. From 2002 to 2003,
our revenue increased from $107.7&nbsp;million to $124.7&nbsp;million, a 16%
increase. For the same period, our total operating expenses increased 6%, from
$101.5&nbsp;million in 2002 to $107.6&nbsp;million in 2003.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman" style="letter-spacing:0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">Our days sales outstanding, or DSO, defined as
ending gross accounts receivable and unbilled revenue divided by the trailing
90&nbsp;days average daily sales, increased slightly from 48&nbsp;days at
December&nbsp;31, 2003 to 49 days at December&nbsp;31, 2004. Our ability to
maintain our DSO is a result of our concerted efforts to work with our
customers at the time of billing remittance to improve payment processing and
approvals and understanding of the billing content and services provided.
Further, we realized a benefit of $3.2 million in 2004 from the collection of
up-front fees related to customer payments in advance for service fees that are
required to be deferred under SAB 104.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman" style="letter-spacing:0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We cannot predict with certainty whether we
will be able to continue to maintain or improve our DSO. If our customers delay
payment to us in the future, our DSO, operating cash flow and cash balances
could be adversely impacted.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Investing
Activities</font></u></i></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our use of cash for investing activities in
2004 included $12.9 million of investments in capital assets and software
development projects, $4.4 million to complete the bmd acquisition in February
2004 and $8.9 million of purchases, net of sales, of low-risk investment
instruments such as commercial paper, municipal bonds and certificates of
deposit. Our software development investments in 2004 totaled $10.1 million,
compared to $5.1 million in 2003 and $8.9&nbsp;million in 2002. The significant
software development efforts in 2004 included our 9-1-1 IM product, which is a
web-based front-end application for our ILEC license customers and our VoIP and
IEN product offerings. The decline in capitalized software investment
activities from $8.9 million in 2002 to $5.1 million in 2003 was attributable
to completion of several of the initiatives undertaken in 2002, most notably
our CDB and IntelliCast product offerings in</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;">&nbsp;</p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">Capital asset purchases of $2.8 million in
2004 related primarily to additional hardware and software investments to
enhance our infrastructure and software applications. We also acquired
additional equipment and software of $3.0 million through capital leases. While
these purchases did not require cash outlays, they did increase our cash
obligations in future periods for both principal and interest payments over the
terms of the leases. These expected outlays are depicted in the table above
that summarizes estimated cash requirements by year.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;">&nbsp;</p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">The $25.3 million utilized in 2002 for
investing activities included a material investment in leasehold improvements
and capital assets for our new corporate facility that totaled approximately
$11.0&nbsp;million. In 2002, we also acquired approximately $5.0&nbsp;million
in capital assets for enhancements to our software applications and network
infrastructure, along with an additional $3.7&nbsp;million in new capital
leases.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Financing Activities</font></u></i></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:0pt;">In 2004, we paid $4.6 million for the second of three payments to NVP
II associated with our contingent purchase obligation. We also repaid $3.2
million on capital lease obligations and paid principal payments of $10.2
million on notes payable to GE Capital, which included the pre-payment of $5.9
million of remaining principal payments in December 2004 for two previous term
loans.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman" style="letter-spacing:0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">An additional source of funds in 2004 was
$3.8 million related to stock option exercises and $894,000 in proceeds from
stock sold through our 1998 Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Given the volatility
of our stock price relative to the weighted average exercise price of the stock
options we have issued in the past, we cannot predict the level to which
additional options will be exercised in future periods or whether they will be exercised
at all. As such, the source of cash from future exercises should not be relied
upon.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2004, we have a
revolving line of credit that is available to meet operating needs. Borrowing
availability may not exceed the lower of: (i)&nbsp;$20.0&nbsp;million; or
(ii)&nbsp;two times adjusted EBITDA (or $49.3 million at December&nbsp;31,
2004) as defined in the line of credit agreement, which was amended in
November&nbsp;2003. The interest rate on amounts borrowed under the line of
credit is equal to the lower of the prime rate plus 1.5%, which was 6.75% as of
December&nbsp;31, 2004, or LIBOR plus 3.75% per annum, which was 5.76% as of
December&nbsp;31, 2004. The line of credit matures on December&nbsp;31, 2006,
requires a $2.0&nbsp;million minimum balance to be maintained and is collateralized
by accounts receivable and certain other assets. As of December&nbsp;31, 2004,
$2.0&nbsp;million was outstanding and $17.2 million was available for
additional borrowings. An additional $850,000 is being utilized to satisfy
letter of credit obligations related to the occupancy of our primary facilities
in Longmont, Colorado and Lisle, Illinois.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also have access to a maximum of $10.0
million through capital lease lines with two entities. The interest rate is
equal to the entities&#146; cost of funds plus an additional interest rate profit at
the time of each lease. Each lease schedule is collateralized by the underlying
assets and is subject to review and approval by the lessor at the time of our
application. Each lease has either a 24-month or a 36-month termination date.
As of December&nbsp;31, 2004, we have utilized approximately $2.8 million of
the $10.0 million available under the capital lease lines.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;19, 2004, we entered into
the Fifth Amendment to our Loan and Security Agreement with General Electric
Capital Corporation in order to ensure that we will have additional flexibility
in conducting domestic and international operations by eliminating the
requirement to obtain the lender&#146;s consent for:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>An acquisition
or acquisitions that, in aggregate, are valued at less than $15.0&nbsp;million;
or</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Inter-company
transfers of funds between us and any foreign subsidiary that, in aggregate,
would exceed a $2.0 million balance at any point in time.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Covenant
Compliance</font></i></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We were in compliance with all debt covenants
as of December&nbsp;31, 2004.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Assessment
of Future Liquidity</font></i></b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based on available cash resources,
anticipated capital expenditures and projected operating cash flow, we believe
that we will be able to adequately fund our operations through at least the
next twelve months. In making this assessment, we have considered:</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Our
consolidated cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of $39.4 million
as of December&nbsp;31, 2004;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
availability of funding under our revolving credit facility;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The anticipated
level of capital expenditures during 2005;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
$4.4&nbsp;million redemption of Preferred Stock, presently held by NV
Partners&nbsp;II LP, to be made in June&nbsp;2005;</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Presently
scheduled debt service requirements during 2005; and</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Our expectation
of realizing positive cash flow from operations through 2005.</p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The availability of borrowings under our
credit facility and lease line of credit is subject to covenants and
limitations that require us to maintain compliance with specified operating and
financial parameters as described earlier. While we were in compliance with all
covenant ratios at December&nbsp;31, 2004, there can be no assurance that we
will continue to be in compliance with these ratios over time, especially if
our debt borrowings increase or our operating results are not sufficient to
cover our fixed financing payments.</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><a name="Item7a_QuantitativeAndQualitative_130353"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 7A.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;
</font>QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</b></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Market risk represents the risk of loss that
may impact our financial position, results of operations or cash flows due to
adverse changes in financial and commodity market prices and rates. We are
exposed to market risk to the extent that United States interest rates change
due to inflation or other factors. This exposure is directly related to our
normal operating and funding activities. The interest payable on our line of
credit is determined based on the lower of prime rate plus 1.5% or LIBOR plus
3.75% per annum, and, therefore, is affected by changes in market interest
rates. Interest rates on our capital lease lines are dependent on interest
rates in effect at the time the lease line is drawn upon. Total liabilities
outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2004 under the line of credit and capital
lease lines were approximately $4.8 million. Based on amounts borrowed as of
December&nbsp;31, 2004, we would have a resulting decline in future annual
earnings and cash flows of approximately $48,000 for every 1% increase in prime
lending rates. We have no plans to use derivative instruments or engage in
hedging activities.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="color:windowtext;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>
